chunks: What has come upon you that you do not spend in the way of God, when the heritage of the heavens and the earth belongs to God? Those of you who spent before the victory and fought, are not equal (to those who did not). They are higher in position than those who spent after (the victory) and fought. To each one God has made the promise of excellence, for God is aware of all you do.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in reward between those who spent before the Conquest and those who spent after it?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of *Fadl al-Sabiqin* (preeminence of the early believers), highlighting the superior merit of those who supported the Prophet during the critical pre-Conquest period in Mecca. It underscores that while all believers are promised reward, the degree of honor is stratified based on the timing and intensity of their sacrifice, reflecting the historical transition from the Meccan to the Medinan phases of Islam.
